profile._note: Curated page text, rendered by the pages at runtime. Strings allow [label](url), **bold** and {{tokens}} (e.g. {{short}}, {{poss}}). Every fact typed here also goes in data/claims_static.json with its source.
profile.lede: A running check of what Tran promised voters in CA-45, what he has done in office, and what he says on the issues people are fighting about. Every entry links to its source.

facts.label: 2026 general

map.heading: CA-45 spans two counties
map.intro: Tran represents cities in both Los Angeles County and Orange County. Prop 50 redrew the lines for the 2026 election. The new map takes effect Jan 3, 2027; until then he represents the 2023 lines.
map.note: Shaded areas are the parts of each city inside the district; the dark line is the district boundary. Boundaries: U.S. Census Bureau TIGERweb (119th and 120th Congressional Districts). Population figures: 2020 Census, from the [California Senate Office of Demographics](https://sdmg.senate.ca.gov/committeehome/2025-congressional-districts/congressional-district-45-2025). Current lines: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/California%27s_45th_congressional_district). [Official boundary map](https://sdmg.senate.ca.gov/sites/sdmg.senate.ca.gov/files/2026-02/cd45_2025.png).

placeStats._note: Residents of each city inside the 2027 district and the share of the city's population, from the California Senate Office of Demographics (2020 Census). 'old' is w (whole) or p (part) when the city was in the 2023-26 district, empty when new.

map.leavingNote: Dropped from the district by Prop 50: Brea, Yorba Linda and Rossmoor. Placentia shrinks to a partial city.

money.watchIntro: Industries tied to his record and committees (Armed Services and Small Business) and to Orange County issues: immigration enforcement, public safety, housing costs, health care and jobs. Each card totals the PACs and donor employers whose names fit the category.
israelNotes: Endorsed by J Street PAC, not AIPAC. No United Democracy Project or DMFI outside spending in CA-45 in 2024.
Not on the August 2025 AIPAC trip to Israel. Took a Feb 13–19, 2026 trip to Israel paid for by the J Street Education Fund ($19,864).
udpNotes: **2024:** UDP's only California House spending was in CA-34 and CA-47. In CA-47 it spent over $4 million, mostly on TV and mailers, against Dave Min before the March primary. Min won anyway. [KQED](https://www.kqed.org/news/12016915/aipac-spent-big-in-the-2024-election-how-did-the-money-show-up-in-californias-congressional-races) [ProPublica](https://projects.propublica.org/itemizer/committee/C00799031/2024/independent-expenditures)

**2026:** FEC independent-expenditure records show no UDP spending for or against Tran. UDP's California money this cycle went to the CA-14 race. [FEC](https://www.fec.gov/data/candidate/H4CA45170/) [Jewish Insider](https://jewishinsider.com/2026/08/aipac-closes-a-rocky-primary-season-with-a-california-gamble/)

**In 2023–24, AIPAC's PAC gave $19,512 to his Republican opponent, Michelle Steel,** and nothing to Tran (total of the itemized gifts dated 2023 and 2024). [ProPublica](https://projects.propublica.org/itemizer/committee/C00704981/pac-donations/C00797670)

Track AIPAC's figure for Tran counts money from pro-Israel donors and PACs; FEC records show most of it came through J Street. It is not UDP spending. [Track AIPAC](https://www.trackaipac.com/tracker/people/member-derek-tran-ca-45-d)
money.outsideNote: A third-party tracker had reported about $1M from the crypto super PAC Fairshake for Tran in 2026; FEC records show no Fairshake spending for or against him.
money.pacsNote: The Jewish Democratic Council of America PAC passed through about $6,600 in 2024; it is not counted as pro-Israel here because Track AIPAC does not count it.

events.intro: Public town halls and forums where Tran answers questions in person, by phone or online, from his press releases and news coverage.

officeHours.heading: Mobile office hours
officeHours.intro: His staff, not Tran himself, hold regular drop-in hours for help with federal agencies: Social Security, Medicare, VA benefits, immigration cases, the IRS and passports. No appointment needed.
officeHours.note: Schedule from [tran.house.gov/mobile-office-hours](https://tran.house.gov/mobile-office-hours). Check there or call the Cypress office before going; dates can change around holidays.

overview._note: Member-specific Overview tiles (scripts/build_overview.py). costPromise: start of the promise 'issue' in data/promises.json whose status answers 'Delivering on cost of living?'; costPledge: how the tile names that pledge (default 'cost-of-living'). themes may add a 'note' after the rule. themes: [{q, rx, section, noun}] counts press releases mentioning a topic (e.g. Luz Rivas: Focused on homelessness?). votes: [{q, roll, section, what}] shows one recorded vote (e.g. the Epstein Files Transparency Act, House roll 2025-289).
